statement.source_mapping: Research/Submission.lean: Research.BlockJacobi.block_jacobi_real formalizes the complete authoritative theorem:block_jacobi_real from /spec/source.txt (paper.tex, selected result), with explicit A = D + N block support, IsUnit D.det, and A * x = b assumptions. The correction and iterate are constructed from the residual, for all initial guesses and all natural dimensions. The conclusions include the update equations, signed error recurrence, power identity, componentwise bound, maximum-row-sum infinity-norm bound, equality of the complex spectral radii under negation, convergence for every initial guess iff rho(P) < 1, and norm-based sufficiency with the contraction inequality. Complex spectral radius is Mathlib spectralRadius of the complexified matrix converted to real; finite matrix spectra are bounded and the empty-dimensional convention is zero. Only the final theorem proof uses sorry as authorized scaffolding. No feedback.json was present; no statement revision was requested or made. /spec/support contains no files, so there are no supplied supporting sources to copy. The fallible plan was used as a checklist without adding assumptions.

requirements.requirement: Define the exact update-form block Jacobi iterates for the stated decomposition.
requirements.evidence: correctionAt(A,D,b,y)=D^(-1)(b-Ay); update(y)=y+correctionAt(y); iterate starts at x₀ and recursively applies this update. Target (1) explicitly asserts D c_k=b-Ay_k and y_(k+1)=y_k+c_k. Its c_k denotes the source correction c^{k+1}, an equivalent index convention. Under nonsingularity, applying the inverse of block-diagonal D is exactly the prescribed block solve.

requirements.requirement: Prove the error identities, componentwise and infinity-norm bounds, and the spectral-radius convergence equivalence.
requirements.evidence: Target (1) asserts e_(k+1)=T e_k, e_k=T^k e_0, the coordinatewise inequality |(e_k)_i|≤((|T|)^k |e_0|)_i, and ||e_k||∞≤||T||∞^k ||e_0||∞ for every x₀,k,i. Targets (2)-(3) assert rho(T)=rho(D^(-1)N) and convergence for every initial vector iff rho(T)<1. Target (4) explicitly supplies convergence and ||U(u)-U(v)||∞≤||T||∞ ||u-v||∞ when 0≤||T||∞<1. The norms have the required maximum-coordinate and maximum-row-sum definitions. The complexified finite matrix has finite spectral radius, so the real conversion preserves it.

requirements.evidence: The theorem uses the specified A,D,N,b,x with A=D+N and Ax=b; T=-D^(-1)N and e_k=iterate(A,D,b,x₀,k)-x. All initial guesses are universal and convergence is to that same specified x. The final Lipschitz bound concerns the actual update U(y)=y+D^(-1)(b-Ay). Block labels encode the original within-block D and off-block N support.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the stated hypotheses and generality. Do not assume the conclusion or introduce a circular definition.
requirements.evidence: The base hypotheses are precisely the decomposition and block support, nonsingularity expressed as det D a unit over R, and Ax=b. There is no additional convergence or spectral premise. The norm condition is only the antecedent of the sufficient-condition conclusion. Arbitrary block labels impose no size or label restrictions. All natural indices and initial vectors are covered. Including dimension zero is consistent: the unique vector sequence converges, both norms and the spectral radius are zero, and the identities hold. Product-topology convergence equals infinity-norm convergence in finite dimensions.
